trigger: launch() wrote in_flight/done bookkeeping AFTER spawn_detached() instead of before
summary: A fast-completing send could have its published done=true clobbered back to false by the launcher's own post-spawn write, silently wedging that one entry forever - empirically reproduced ~1-in-1000 in a standalone harness.

trigger: offer() mismatch branch (head changed under a stalled send - an ordinary coalesce/withdrawal) never reclaimed the slot once the orphaned worker finished
summary: in_flight stayed permanently true against an event_id that could never recur, wedging the ENTIRE outbox (both lanes at the time) for the life of the process. Independently found by security-guardian and cpp-safety.

trigger: mark_batch_sent() now runs on the detached send-executor thread, not the drain-worker thread; guardian_lifecycle_journal.hpp CONCURRENCY paragraph did not name this caller
summary: Doc-comment drift (not a correctness bug - KvStore already serializes its single connection); fixed by naming the caller explicitly in the CONCURRENCY paragraph.

trigger: io_detail::spawn_detached's own documented bad_alloc possibility was not caught in launch()
summary: A thread-creation OOM would propagate uncaught into drain_log_unlocked's catch and be miscounted as an entry-specific send exception rather than a launch failure.

trigger: send_guardian_outbox_entry's comment claimed lifetime safety via synchronous join, which item 4 removed
summary: Comment now contradicted the code (Standing Rule 3); fixed to attribute safety to the orphan-exit contract instead.

trigger: launch() had no try/catch wrapping the risky ticket/lambda/spawn sequence, unlike guardian_io_executor.hpp::run()
summary: Same underlying issue as p1-spawn-detached-bad-alloc-miscounted, raised independently by a second reviewer; fixed together.

trigger: GuardianOutboxSendExecutor had no direct/isolated unit test, unlike GuardianIoExecutor
summary: Fixed: new file tests/unit/test_guardian_outbox_send_executor.cpp added, including the mismatch/reclaim regression case.

trigger: docs/test-coverage.md not updated for the item-4 change
summary: Fixed: entries updated for the drain-worker test additions and the new send-executor test file.

trigger: §3 row 1 cited line numbers that matched the working tree but the sentence claimed verification against a specific SHA where the numbers differed
summary: Fixed: wording clarified to state verification against "this PR's own tree" rather than the specific historical SHA.

trigger: A pre-existing test comment and docs/test-coverage.md entry both described stop()'s join as "a blocking wait on a send that may be blackholed" - no longer true post-fix (bounded to kGuardianSendOfferWait)
summary: Fixed: both comments updated to describe the join as bounded, not indefinite, while noting the underlying persist-before-join property is unchanged.

trigger: One shared GuardianOutboxSendExecutor instance served both the lifecycle log and the compliance/health log
summary: A slow-but-succeeding lifecycle send made the compliance drain_log_unlocked call hit the same executor's mismatch-orphan branch and return Retain without the compliance send ever being invoked - silent, repeated starvation of an entire Guardian audit lane. security-guardian separately classified this as I1 (audit control failure) in the round-2+3 re-review, not merely I5.

trigger: One active_worker_count()==0 assertion in the new test file was not wrapped in spin_until, unlike every other instance in the same file
summary: Empirically reproducible (2-7/20000 iterations, worse under TSan); found independently by happy-path and Gate 8 cpp-expert. Fixed.

trigger: guardian_engine.cpp's wire_spark_engine comment claimed mark_batch_sent "does not appear in [the CONCURRENCY paragraph] by name" after the same PR's own edit had just named it
summary: Self-contradiction introduced within this PR; fixed.

waiver_rationale: Fix empirically broke test_guardian_engine_spark_reconcile.cpp's "pending records are durable BEFORE stop() joins the drain worker" test by shrinking the observable still-joining window below the test's polling granularity. The underlying property that test guards (persist-before-join) is unaffected by this file either way; only the join's duration would have shrunk. Cost of the SHOULD finding (bounded, already-small per-shutdown latency) judged smaller than the risk of redesigning a load-bearing pre-existing test under this PR's time budget.
trigger: stop() did not wake a caller parked in offer()'s wait_until, unlike guardian_io_executor.hpp::run()
summary: Up to kGuardianSendOfferWait of avoidable shutdown latency. Built and wired, then REVERTED after it made stop() fast enough to race ahead of a pre-existing durability-ordering test's own polling window; left as a documented trade-off note.

trigger: offer()'s reclaim path on a mismatched orphan discards a thrown eptr with no counter/log
summary: Diagnostic-signal narrowing versus pre-item-4 behavior (where the same race's throw was always counted via drain_log_unlocked's catch). Not a correctness bug - the orphaned result belongs to a superseded entry with nowhere correct to attribute it. Accepted as documented behavior, not actioned separately.

trigger: No heartbeat tag/counter/log exists for "a send has been stalled for N seconds"
summary: A loud pre-fix hang is traded for a silent post-fix slow-drain with no operator-visible signal once this ships live at the F14 flip. Recommended before F14, tracked the same way row 3 tracks #3816's "Detection signal: none today."

waiver_rationale: Fix empirically broke test_guardian_outbox_drain_worker.cpp's "R4: a refill re-arm does not wait out the periodic bound" test - waking loop() on every completed send raced ahead of that test's own internal-refill-only observable. Cost of the SHOULD finding (a cadence interval's worth of latency on an already-rare slow-but-healthy send, unreachable in production today) judged smaller than the risk of redesigning a second load-bearing pre-existing test under this PR's time budget.
trigger: On an offer() timeout, the drain worker is not woken when the delayed send later completes - it waits for the next enqueue or the periodic backstop
summary: Degrades a merely-slow-but-healthy connection's delivery cadence, not just a dead one. A completion-waker fix was built and wired, then REVERTED after it broke a pre-existing refill-rearm timing test; left as a documented trade-off note.

trigger: No governance.d/ ledger fragment existed for this fix at review time
summary: This fragment is the fix - generated before push, per CLAUDE.md's own evidence-fragment rule.

trigger: No changelog.d/ fragment for a dormant-but-real fix, breaking this exact series' own precedent (#2237, #2270 both shipped fragments for equally-dormant fixes)
summary: compliance-officer independently raised the same recommendation. Fixed: fragment added.

trigger: Round 1's bookkeeping-before-spawn fix placed the in_flight_event_id string copy-assignment BEFORE the try block that round 1 itself added
summary: A bad_alloc on that specific string copy would still leave in_flight=true uncaught - the same permanent-wedge class round 1 closed everywhere else, one statement outside the guarded region. Fixed by moving the whole bookkeeping block inside the try.

trigger: UP-1's fix (the two-lane split) had no regression test at the GuardianOutboxDrainWorker layer where the bug actually lived, only isolated GuardianOutboxSendExecutor coverage
summary: Fixed: added, mutation-verified RED against the pre-round-2 single-executor code (first draft used a bounded stall and was vacuous - had to redesign to an indefinite CV-controlled stall to actually discriminate the two designs).

trigger: The Lifecycle-vs-Compliance/Health domain-to-log separation the two-lane routing depends on is enforced only by convention (3 construction sites), not asserted
summary: Holds today by inspection; a future misrouted entry could silently reintroduce the starvation class. Not actioned - NICE, no current path.

trigger: Recording the p2-up1 defect's severity classification for the ledger
summary: The pre-round-2 shared-executor bug silently starved Guardian compliance/health AUDIT event delivery, not just availability - should re-derive at CRITICAL (not just HIGH) once the send path goes live at the flip (E0/E3 replaces today's E4). Already fixed; recorded for future re-derivation.

trigger: Splitting into two independently-scheduled executors makes same-pass cross-lane wire reordering reachable in a way the single shared executor structurally prevented
summary: A compliance/health event can now appear on the wire between two lifecycle-log entries under concurrent load. GuardianSparkRuntime::drain()'s own header comment already discloses this exact residual as best-effort elsewhere; this adds a second path to an already-documented non-guarantee. Not actioned.
